children.name: heroTitle
children.content: To develop the world’s best quantum technology to solve the world’s most complex problems.

rawBlockNode.name: aboutP1
rawBlockNode.content: Founded in 2015 by Dr. Chris Monroe and Dr. Jungsang Kim, IonQ emerged from more than 30 years of academic research and foundational breakthroughs licensed from the University of Maryland and Duke University. With early support from global venture capital firm New Enterprise Associates and the goal of bringing trapped ion quantum computing out of the lab and into real-world use, IonQ has since grown into a global leader in quantum computing, networking, and sensing.

rawBlockNode.name: aboutP2
rawBlockNode.content: IonQ has established partnerships with leading academic institutions, industry innovators, and federal agencies, and continues to advance one of the most aggressive technology roadmaps in the field. Our mission is to solve problems that are beyond the reach of classical systems.

rawBlockNode.name: para32
rawBlockNode.content: We are accelerating our technology and commercial roadmap toward world’s most powerful quantum systems for practical innovation in chemistry, logistics, financial modeling, cybersecurity, and defense.

rawBlockNode.content: IonQ’s trapped ion quantum systems are designed to solve challenges no classical computer can touch—from logistics and drug discovery to national defense.

rawBlockNode.name: pre
rawBlockNode.content: Quantum built on nature’s most perfect building block:

children.name: heroSub
children.content: IonQ’s trapped ion quantum systems are designed to solve challenges no classical computer can touch—from logistics and drug discovery to national defense.

children.name: pre
children.content: Quantum built on nature’s most perfect building block:

children.name: col1t
children.content:
At its core, a quantum computer is a machine that uses a quantum system, like the spin of an electron, to do a very specific type of math.

This math takes advantage of the uniquely complex behavior of quantum systems, namely entanglement and superposition, to perform calculations that are fundamentally unlike the calculations ordinary computers based on classical physics can perform.

children.name: col2t
children.content:
Many quantum hardware developers use "synthetic" quantum systems for their quantum bits (qubits for short), like loops of superconducting wire, intentional imperfections in crystalline silicon, or other designs carefully coaxed to behave as quantum systems.

At IonQ, we take a different approach. We use a naturally occurring quantum system: individual atoms.

children.name: col3t
children.content:
These atoms are the heart of our quantum processing units. We trap them in 3D space, and then use lasers to do everything from initial preparation to final readout.

It requires counterintuitive physics, precision optical and mechanical engineering, and fine-grained firmware control over a variety of components, but the superior results speak for themselves.

rawBlockNode.name: intro
rawBlockNode.content: Most quantum computers rely on superconducting circuits or exotic materials. IonQ takes a simpler, more powerful approach: we use single atoms—identical, stable, and natural—as the building blocks of computation.

children.name: pBody1
children.content: The most important part of any quantum computer are its quantum bits, or qubits. IonQ’s qubits are ionized ytterbium atoms, a silvery rare-earth metal. Each ytterbium atom is perfectly identical to every other ytterbium atom in the universe.

children.name: pBody2
children.content: Moreover, once prepared in a particular stable quantum state, they can remain in that state for very long periods of time — they’re so consistent they’re used in one of the most accurate atomic clocks ever built.

children.name: aboutP1
children.content: Founded in 2015 by Dr. Chris Monroe and Dr. Jungsang Kim, IonQ emerged from more than 30 years of academic research and foundational breakthroughs licensed from the University of Maryland and Duke University. With early support from global venture capital firm New Enterprise Associates and the goal of bringing trapped ion quantum computing out of the lab and into real-world use, IonQ has since grown into a global leader in quantum computing, networking, and sensing.

children.name: aboutP2
children.content: IonQ has established partnerships with leading academic institutions, industry innovators, and federal agencies, and continues to advance one of the most aggressive technology roadmaps in the field. Our mission is to solve problems that are beyond the reach of classical systems.

children.name: para32
children.content: We are accelerating our technology and commercial roadmap toward world’s most powerful quantum systems for practical innovation in chemistry, logistics, financial modeling, cybersecurity, and defense.
